messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.cli.bug.BugCLI162Test.testInfiniteLoop()
  - It configures HelpFormatter with width 20 and calls printHelp("app", options) where options contain a long description (“This is a looooong description”). The comment says “used to hang & crash”, i.e., this is a regression test for CLI-162.

- Code path:
  - HelpFormatter.printHelp(String, Options) delegates to printHelp(PrintWriter, ...).
  - That calls printOptions(...), which builds the options help text and wraps descriptions.
  - Wrapping is handled by renderWrappedText(StringBuffer, int, int, String), which drives the line breaking via findWrapPos(String, int, int).

- Core wrapping logic (renderWrappedText):
  - It computes an initial wrap position pos = findWrapPos(text, width, 0).
  - If no wrap is needed (pos == -1), it appends the text and returns.
  - Otherwise, it appends the first line up to pos and then enters a loop:
    - lastPos = pos
    - It creates the next chunk as text = padding + text.substring(pos).trim(), where padding is a string of spaces equal to nextLineTabStop (indent for wrapped lines).
    - It then recomputes pos = findWrapPos(text, width, 0).
    - If pos == -1, it appends the remaining text and returns.
    - Otherwise, it appends text.substring(0, pos), adds a newline, and repeats.

- Root cause of the infinite loop:
  - When the remainder begins with an unbreakable long word that cannot fit into a line of the given width after indentation, the only whitespace character within the first width characters is located in the artificially added padding at the beginning of the line.
  - findWrapPos scans backward from startPos + width to find the last whitespace at or before that boundary. In this case, it finds the last whitespace inside the padding (i.e., at the end of the indentation).
  - That means pos points into the padding area (roughly equal to the padding length). renderWrappedText then appends text.substring(0, pos), which consists solely of spaces; rtrim removes them, so it appends an empty line.
  - The remainder text does not progress: text = padding + text.substring(pos).trim() effectively reconstructs the same “padding + longword...” string, because pos was in the padding. On the next iteration, findWrapPos returns the same pos again.
  - Without a progress check, the loop runs forever, continuously appending empty lines, leading to a hang and eventual OutOfMemoryError, exactly as described in the bug report.

- Evidence in code:
  - renderWrappedText has a while(true) loop that recomputes pos on a padded string. This is where progress can stall if the wrap point falls inside the padding.
  - findWrapPos attempts to find a break before startPos + width by scanning for whitespace; when none exist in the content portion, it picks the whitespace in the padding, causing the non-progress scenario.

- Existing mitigation:
  - In the code version shown, renderWrappedText includes a defensive check: if (pos == lastPos) { throw new RuntimeException("Text too long for line - throwing exception to avoid infinite loop [CLI-162]: " + text); }
  - This explicitly detects the “no forward progress” condition and aborts to prevent the infinite loop (a direct fix for CLI-162).
  - The historical failure (hang/crash) occurs when this guard is absent; the test was introduced to ensure the formatter no longer loops infinitely for such inputs.

Conclusion:
The infinite loop stems from renderWrappedText’s wrapping loop when dealing with a long, unbreakable word and a narrow width plus indentation. findWrapPos selects a break inside the synthetic padding, so the loop doesn’t consume any content and repeats forever. The fix is to ensure forward progress (as shown by the pos == lastPos guard) or to adjust the wrapping to avoid breaking within the padding (e.g., by using an appropriate startPos or handling overlong tokens explicitly).

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).

HelpFormatter.renderWrappedText(StringBuffer, int, int, String)
HelpFormatter.findWrapPos(String, int, int)
